title: Location Tracking & GPS Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to stop apps from tracking your location. Disable GPS tracking, audit app permissions, and protect your privacy from geolocation surveillance.
intro: Your location is one of your most sensitive pieces of data. Apps, services, and governments can track where you go, when you're there, and build detailed profiles of your daily life. This checklist helps you audit and disable unwanted location tracking across all your devices.

items.task: Turn off system-wide location services
items.why: Prevents all apps from accessing GPS data unless you specifically enable it per app
items.howTo: iOS: Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > Off. Android: Settings > Location > Use location > Off. Re-enable only for essential apps like maps or weather.

items.task: Review location permissions for all installed apps
items.why: Many apps request location access they don't need for core functionality
items.howTo: Check each app's location permission. Set to 'Never' for unnecessary apps, 'While Using App' for others, avoid 'Always' unless critical. Remove apps that won't work without location if not needed.

items.task: Turn off precise location for non-essential apps
items.why: Gives approximate location instead of exact GPS coordinates, reducing tracking accuracy
items.howTo: iOS: In Location Services, tap each app and toggle off 'Precise Location'. Android: In app permissions, choose 'Approximate location' instead of 'Precise location'.

items.task: Disable location history and timeline features
items.why: Prevents creation of detailed movement logs that can be subpoenaed or hacked
items.howTo: Google: myactivity.google.com > Location History > Turn off. Apple: Settings > Privacy > Location Services > System Services > Significant Locations > Off.

items.task: Turn off location-based advertising
items.why: Stops advertisers from targeting you based on places you visit
items.howTo: iOS: Settings > Privacy > Location Services > System Services > Location-Based Apple Ads > Off. Android: Settings > Google > Ads > Opt out of Ads Personalization.

items.task: Review Find My Device settings
items.why: Balance security benefits with privacy concerns, especially for shared family accounts
items.howTo: Keep enabled for theft protection but review who can see your location. iOS: Settings > [Name] > Find My. Android: Settings > Security > Find My Device.

items.task: Turn off location sharing in social media apps
items.why: Prevents broadcasting your location to followers and prevents apps from building location profiles
items.howTo: Facebook: Settings > Privacy > Location Services > Off. Instagram: Settings > Privacy > Location Services > Off. Twitter: Privacy and safety > Location information > Off.

items.task: Disable geotagging in camera and photo apps
items.why: Photos with location data can reveal your home, work, and travel patterns when shared
items.howTo: Turn off location access for camera app. iOS: Settings > Privacy > Location Services > Camera > Never. Android: Camera app settings > Location tags > Off.

items.task: Set weather apps to manual location entry
items.why: Weather apps often track continuously when they only need your general area occasionally
items.howTo: Change weather app settings to manually enter your city instead of auto-detecting. Use 'While Using App' permission instead of 'Always' if auto-detection needed.

items.task: Configure map apps for privacy
items.why: Map apps need location but can be configured to minimize tracking and data retention
items.howTo: Google Maps: Turn off location history, delete past timeline data. Use Incognito mode. Apple Maps: Settings > Privacy > Location Services > Apple Maps > While Using App only.

items.task: Limit location precision on dating apps
items.why: Prevents stalking and exact location triangulation while still enabling matching
items.howTo: Use approximate location settings. Avoid apps that require precise GPS. Consider location spoofing tools for additional protection. Review distance settings regularly.

items.task: Block location access for websites
items.why: Websites can track your location for advertising and profiling without clear benefit to you
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Site Settings > Location > Don't allow. Firefox: about:preferences#privacy > Permissions > Location > Settings > Block new requests. Use Incognito Browser for automatic blocking.

items.task: Use VPN to mask your IP-based location
items.why: Your IP address reveals your approximate location to every website you visit
items.howTo: Choose a reputable VPN service with no-logs policy. Connect to servers in different locations. Avoid free VPNs that may sell your data. Test for IP leaks regularly.

items.task: Use privacy-focused search engines
items.why: Google and Bing track searches and correlate them with your location data
items.howTo: Switch to DuckDuckGo, Startpage, or Brave Search. These don't track or store your search location. Set as default search engine in your browser.

items.task: Enable WiFi MAC address randomization
items.why: Stores and public WiFi can track your device's unique identifier to monitor your movements
items.howTo: iOS: Settings > WiFi > Private WiFi Address > On for each network. Android: Settings > WiFi > Privacy > Use randomized MAC. Avoid auto-connecting to public WiFi.

items.task: Delete existing location history from major services
items.why: Years of stored location data can be accessed by law enforcement or hackers
items.howTo: Google: myactivity.google.com > Delete activity by > All time > Location History. Apple: Settings > Privacy > Analytics & Improvements > Delete Analytics Data. Review other services you use.

items.task: Disable Bluetooth when not needed
items.why: Bluetooth beacons in stores and public spaces can track your movements even without internet
items.howTo: Turn off Bluetooth in settings when not using wireless devices. iOS: Settings > Bluetooth > Off. Android: Settings > Connected devices > Bluetooth > Off.

items.task: Review vehicle tracking settings
items.why: Modern cars collect detailed location data that can be shared with manufacturers and third parties
items.howTo: Check your car's privacy settings and connected services. Opt out of data sharing programs. Consider disconnecting from manufacturer apps if location tracking can't be disabled.

items.task: Audit location tracking on smart home devices
items.why: Smart speakers, security cameras, and IoT devices often track and report location data
items.howTo: Review privacy settings for Alexa, Google Home, smart thermostats, and security systems. Disable location-based features you don't use. Check what data is being shared.

items.task: Configure fitness trackers and health apps for privacy
items.why: Fitness apps create detailed maps of your running routes, gym visits, and daily patterns
items.howTo: Turn off route tracking and map sharing features. Set activities to private. Avoid posting workout locations on social features. Review third-party data sharing settings.

items.task: Balance emergency location services with privacy
items.why: Some location services are important for safety but can be configured to minimize routine tracking
items.howTo: Keep emergency SOS location enabled but disable routine emergency location sharing. Review which contacts can see your location in emergency apps. Test that emergency services still work.

pro_tips: Use airplane mode with WiFi to prevent GPS tracking while still accessing the internet when you need maximum location privacy
Regularly audit your Google Timeline and Apple's Significant Locations to see exactly how much location data is being collected
Consider using a Faraday bag or turning off your phone completely when attending sensitive meetings or locations
Check if your employer or school has mobile device management that could be tracking your location through work/school apps
Be aware that even with location services off, cell tower triangulation can still approximate your location - only airplane mode prevents this completely
